name: EP250207b field (Hubble)
blurb: The field of EP250207b, a fast X-ray transient, seen by Hubble.
label: ep250207b-hubble
story: Hubble returned to this spot to follow the fading light of EP250207b, a brief flash of X-rays caught by the Einstein Probe that astronomers think may have come from the merger of two compact objects. Its likely home is a nearby lenticular galaxy whose stars show no signs of recent star formation.

claims.text: EP250207b is a fast X-ray transient discovered by the Einstein Probe
Its properties favor an origin in a binary compact object merger
Its candidate host is a nearby lenticular galaxy with no signs of recent star formation
The candidate host galaxy is WISEA J111002.65-075211.9
Hubble program 17806 imaged EP250207b to follow its light curve
Hubble program 17806 follows kilonovae from merger-driven gamma-ray bursts
